key_insight: Turn-level best-of-N sampling improves LLM agent accuracy and consistency by selecting among multiple candidate actions before each execution.
engineering_relevance: A generator-selector setup offers a practical inference-time scaling approach for agents tackling complex, long-horizon terminal tasks.
method: Generate N candidate actions at each turn.
Use a second, off-the-shelf open-weight LLM to compare candidates and select one.
Execute the selected action and repeat.
evidence_signal: Experiments on long-horizon terminal tasks report 5–10% accuracy improvements and greater consistency across repeated attempts, with trajectory analysis indicating better instruction following, debugging, and testing.
watch_item: Generating and comparing multiple actions per turn adds inference cost; the abstract does not quantify latency or cost-effectiveness.
paper_title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
